items.answer: Field of view (FOV) is a content-related factor in virtual reality (VR) that affects susceptibility to cybersickness (CS), and it is the extent to which the display in a VR headset captures the user's field of vision.

The type of transition, meaning how the scene changes from one field of view to another, is another aspect of locomotion that affects cybersickness (CS); teleportation, an instantaneous transition, is found to reduce cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement such as walking, running, and jumping.
The output of cybersickness (CS) measurement can be binary classes, multiple classes, or a sickness score that is a number.
Content-based inputs for measuring cybersickness (CS) include optical flow, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity.

One way to perform machine learning-based (ML) evaluation of cybersickness (CS) is to use transparent models, which provide clear insight into the decision-making process and whose inner workings can easily be understood.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.
